html:
German East Africa was the German colony that covered what are now mainland Tanzania, Rwanda and Burundi, begun in 1885 when Carl Peters's company won an imperial charter for treaties he had made with chiefs.

Coastal resistance in the Abushiri revolt led the German state to take over in 1891, with its capital at Dar es Salaam. Forced cotton growing, taxes and harsh rule led to the Maji Maji rebellion, after which the Germans built railways and schools.

In the First World War the German commander Paul von Lettow-Vorbeck fought a long campaign against British forces, and many African porters died. After the war, Britain took Tanganyika as a League of Nations mandate, and Belgium took Ruanda-Urundi.
sum: German East Africa was the German colony that covered what are now mainland Tanzania, Rwanda and Burundi, begun in 1885 when Carl Peters's company won an imperial charter for treaties he had made with chiefs.
